name: Core42
snippet: G42's cloud and compute arm runs the UAE's sovereign cloud with Microsoft and AI clusters in the US and Europe. It tripled its New York site to 60 MW in June 2026.

facts.label: Abu Dhabi government entities on its sovereign cloud
Stargate UAE first phase (G42)
facts.value: 200 MW of NVIDIA GB300 planned for 2026

origin: Core42 formed in 2023 when G42 combined its cloud unit G42 Cloud, its Inception research unit and its ICT services company Injazat. G42 is the Abu Dhabi AI group backed by national security adviser Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan. In 2024 G42 cut its Chinese technology ties to gain access to US AI chips, and Microsoft invested $1.5B in G42. Core42 became the group's infrastructure business, running Abu Dhabi's sovereign cloud and building GPU and Cerebras clusters at home and in the US.
today: Core42 expanded its deployment at TeraWulf's Lake Mariner campus near Buffalo, New York by 42 MW in June 2026, taking the site from 18 MW to 60 MW. The Lake Mariner lease dates from February 2025 and runs for 10 years, with an option on about 135 MW more. In May 2026 Core42 leased 20 MW in a converted office building in downtown Minneapolis, and its other US sites sit in Dallas, Sunnyvale and Stockton. The company opened a European headquarters in Dublin in 2025, runs deployments in France and Italy, and says it has 10 operational sites. HSBC provided $550M of trade finance in February and May 2026 to fund deployments in the US and Europe. At home, more than 47 Abu Dhabi government entities use its sovereign enabled public cloud built on Microsoft Azure, and in October 2026 it launched a partner program with more than 50 partners. Talal Al Kaissi leads the company as chief executive.
platform: Core42 launched the Core42 AI Cloud in October 2025, a self-service console that rents NVIDIA H100 capacity by the hour or on term commitments for training, fine-tuning and inference. Its Maximus cluster runs AMD Instinct MI300 hardware and ranks in the top 20 of the TOP500 list, and it builds the Condor Galaxy supercomputers with Cerebras. For government and regulated clients it wraps Microsoft Azure with UAE data residency and monitoring controls through its Insight platform, and it sells model access through Compass on a token basis.
outlook: G42 builds Stargate UAE, a 1 GW cluster that OpenAI and Oracle will operate with NVIDIA GB300 systems, and the first NVIDIA chips for the project reached the UAE in May 2026. In September 2026 Reuters reported that the UAE is redesigning the wider 5 GW campus as a network of dispersed sites after Iranian attacks on Gulf infrastructure, and G42 says the specifications remain under review. The US moved the UAE to a more trusted export tier in July 2026, which removes per-shipment licenses for approved firms including G42 and Core42. G42 also plans an 8 exaflop Cerebras supercomputer in India and a $1B sovereign AI project in Vietnam.

Stargate UAE is a G42 project built by G42 and operated by OpenAI and Oracle, so the profile does not credit it to Core42 directly. The Reuters articles could not be fetched and are cited from their headlines and secondary coverage. The aka G42 Cloud refers to the predecessor unit merged into Core42.

name: Humain
ownership: Owned by the Public Investment Fund
snippet: Saudi Arabia's state AI company builds data centers for NVIDIA, AMD and partner clouds. It targets 250 MW by the end of 2026 and a 1.7 GW build in 2027.

facts.label: Launched
facts.value: May 2025 by the Public Investment Fund

facts.label: NVIDIA GPU plan
facts.value: Up to 600,000 GPUs over three years (November 2025)

facts.label: Capacity target
facts.value: 250 MW by end of 2026, 1.7 GW build in 2027

facts.label: AMD, Cisco joint venture
facts.value: MI355X live August 2026, 1 GW target by 2030

origin: The Public Investment Fund launched Humain on May 12, 2025, with a mandate to build Saudi Arabia's full AI stack from data centers to Arabic language models. Tareq Amin leads it as chief executive. The next day NVIDIA agreed to supply 18,000 GB300 chips for a first phase and several hundred thousand GPUs over five years toward 500 MW of capacity. Humain signed AWS, Qualcomm and Groq in the same launch week.
today: Humain says it will reach 250 MW of data center capacity by the end of 2026 and plans a 1.7 GW build in 2027, with targets of about 3 GW by 2030 and 6 GW by 2034. In November 2025 it expanded its NVIDIA deal to up to 600,000 GPUs over three years, and the US authorized GB300-class chip exports to the company. Its first NVIDIA shipment arrived at the end of December 2025. The AMD and Cisco joint venture switched on AMD Instinct MI355X systems in August 2026 and plans 250 MW of MI400 series capacity in the second half of 2027. Humain and xAI plan a 500 MW data center, and Humain invested $3B in xAI's Series E round in February 2026. AWS plans up to 50 MW for a Riyadh AI Zone by 2028, and Humain added Together AI as a cloud partner in August 2026. It is raising a $2.5B data center fund and plans listings in Riyadh and New York by 2029.
platform: Humain builds and owns data centers and leases the compute to anchor tenants such as xAI and AWS, while it also sells its own AI services. Humain One, launched in October 2025, is an enterprise AI platform built with Groq, EY and Replit. Groq runs OpenAI's gpt-oss models for Humain inside its Saudi data centers. Humain also offers the ALLaM Arabic model through Amazon Bedrock and released the humain-m3 model, developed with MiniMax, in September 2026.
outlook: Humain's chief executive says about 80% of its capital goes to data centers, and he puts build costs at $10M to $12M per MW. Its growth depends on US export licenses, which Saudi Arabia receives case by case rather than through the standing tier the UAE won in July 2026. Several large partner sites are years away, including the 100 MW NEOM project with DataVolt due in 2028, and the stc joint venture of up to 1 GW is not yet final. Humain also seeks outside capital as the Public Investment Fund tightens spending.

The AMD deal is a joint venture with AMD and Cisco targeting 1 GW by 2030, not a 500 MW JV as in the seed. name: SK Telecom
ownership: Public (KRX: 017670, NYSE: SKM), part of SK Group
snippet: The Korean mobile operator rents Blackwell GPUs through its Haein cloud and builds AI data centers with AWS and NVIDIA. AI data center revenue rose 92.5% in Q2 2026.

facts.label: SK Horizon investment from KKR and IMM
Ulsan AI data center with AWS

origin: SK Telecom entered GPU cloud in 2024, when it invested in Lambda and agreed to host a Lambda GPU cluster at SK Broadband's Gasan data center in Seoul. It launched its own GPU as a service in January 2025 and opened the Haein cluster of NVIDIA B200 GPUs in August 2025. In June 2025 SK Group and AWS agreed to build South Korea's largest AI data center in Ulsan, a project the Korean government valued at $5B.
today: SK Telecom's AI data center revenue reached KRW 136.2B in the second quarter of 2026, up 92.5% from a year earlier, and the company credits higher utilization at sites such as Gasan. In July 2026 it set a target of 15 GW of AI data center capacity in Korea by 2035, with 5 GW coming online in phases from 2029 and more than 2 GW in the southeast around Ulsan. A new subsidiary, SK Hyper, leads that gigawatt-scale build. In August 2026 SK Telecom moved its existing data centers into a new company, SK Horizon, and sold 49% to KKR and an IMM-led consortium for KRW 3.08T ($2.24B). SK Horizon holds eight operating data centers plus Ulsan and Guro under construction, for 318 MW in total. In June 2026 SK Telecom became an NVIDIA Cloud Partner and plans a gigawatt-scale AI cloud whose first AI factory opens in 2027. Under NVIDIA's October 2025 plan for more than 260,000 GPUs in Korea, SK Group receives more than 50,000 GPUs and SK Telecom provides a manufacturing cloud on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell servers.
platform: SK Telecom sells GPU capacity on demand from the Haein cluster, which joins more than 1,000 Blackwell GPUs and uses VAST Data storage. In July 2026 Haein became the first Blackwell-based AI cloud in Korea to earn the government's CSAP security certification, which opens public sector work. SK Telecom also builds its own A.X models for the government's sovereign foundation model project and runs the 519B parameter A.X K1 on Rebellions neural processors. It leads one of three consortia picked in August 2026 for the government's free AI for All service.
outlook: The Ulsan data center with AWS is due to start operations in the second half of 2027. SK Telecom expects the SK Horizon deal to close in the first quarter of 2027, pending regulatory approval. SK Telecom puts the cost of a single 1 GW-class facility at about KRW 70T, so the 15 GW plan depends on outside capital such as the KKR and IMM deal. In July 2026 NVIDIA and SK Group also announced an initiative worth more than $500B that includes 2 GW of data center capacity.

name: Naver Cloud
snippet: Naver's cloud arm holds Korea's largest NVIDIA allocation, more than 60,000 GPUs, and builds a gigawatt AI factory in Sejong backed by $1B from NVIDIA and up to $9B from Brookfield.

facts.label: GAK Sejong AI factory
facts.value: 55 MW in H1 2027, 200 MW by 2028, 1 GW goal

origin: Naver Cloud runs the cloud and data center business of Naver, the Korean internet company, and builds its HyperCLOVA X language models. It operates Naver's GAK data centers in Chuncheon and Sejong. NVIDIA's October 2025 plan to supply more than 260,000 GPUs to Korea gave Naver Cloud more than 60,000, the largest share of any company. Naver Cloud also serves as one of three cloud providers for the government's National AI Computing Center, alongside NHN Cloud and Kakao.
today: In June 2026 Naver and NVIDIA agreed to turn the GAK Sejong data center into a gigawatt-scale AI factory on NVIDIA's DSX platform, starting at 55 MW in the first half of 2027 and reaching 200 MW by 2028. NVIDIA then agreed in July 2026 to invest $1B for a 4.5% stake in Naver, and Brookfield offered up to $9B of financing for the build. The Sejong expansion is planned to hold about 100,000 Vera Rubin and Blackwell GPUs. Also in June 2026, the Ministry of Science and ICT picked Naver Cloud with Samsung SDS and Elice Group for a KRW 2.08T GPU program, and Naver Cloud's share is 3,112 B300 and 1,008 Vera Rubin GPUs. B300 service starts in 2026 and Vera Rubin service in the first half of 2027. In September 2026 Naver Cloud won a government cybersecurity AI project and began work on AI for military networks.
platform: Naver Cloud Platform sells GPU servers, Kubernetes, storage and access to HyperCLOVA X, which Naver fine-tunes with NVIDIA Nemotron models. AMD agreed in March 2026 to give Naver Cloud early access to Instinct MI455X GPUs and to optimize its AI services on the ROCm software stack. LG CNS supplies liquid cooling for the Sejong AI factory.
outlook: Naver Cloud lost its place in the government's sovereign foundation model project in January 2026, when it failed to advance past the first round, and it declined to bid in the retender. Overseas, it signed a GPU cloud and AI factory partnership with Vietnam's FPT in October 2026 and works with HanmiGlobal on data center projects in Saudi Arabia. Its Morocco plan shrank after the June 2025 announcement of a 500 MW campus. The Nexus Core Systems project now targets 36 MW with construction from 2027, and recent coverage does not spell out Naver's role.

editor_notes: The 60,000 GPU figure is confirmed as more than 60,000 in NVIDIA's October 2025 release. The Saudi Arabia link is real (a Naver Innovation joint venture with the National Housing Company and an April 2026 data center partnership with HanmiGlobal), but I found no signed Saudi GPU cloud contract. Thailand is a May 2025 Thai language model partnership with Siam AI, not a data center. Morocco began as a 500 MW plan with NVIDIA, Nexus Core Systems and Lloyds Capital in June 2025, and an April 2026 revision lists 36 MW without detailing Naver's role. The founding year 2009, the former NBP name, the GAK Chuncheon site and the product list (GPU servers, Kubernetes, storage, CLOVA Studio model access) come from general knowledge of the company and are not in the listed sources. AMD MI455X is early access and Vera Rubin service starts in 2027, so neither is in general use in 2026. The Brookfield and NVIDIA investment press releases could not be fetched and rest on Korea Times coverage.

name: Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison
ownership: Public (IDX: ISAT), controlled by Ooredoo and CK Hutchison
snippet: Indonesian telco whose Lintasarta unit rents H100s as GPU Merdeka. Its new Zankore platform with Ooredoo and NVIDIA targets 1 GW, starting with 200 MW in the first half of 2027.
origin: Indosat's ICT arm Lintasarta launched GPU Merdeka in August 2024, a GPU cloud of NVIDIA H100 servers that Indosat calls a sovereign AI factory. It runs at a BDx Indonesia data center, and NVIDIA says Lintasarta built it in less than three months. Indosat also backs Sahabat-AI, an Indonesian language model that GoTo uses in its Dira voice assistant.
today: In August 2026 Indosat launched Zankore with Ooredoo, NVIDIA and Nokia, an AI factory platform that targets 1 GW of NVIDIA capacity within three years and starts with about 200 MW of GB300 NVL72 systems in the first half of 2027. Ooredoo commits $800M over five years for a 49% stake, and Zankore raised a $3.1B term loan in September 2026. In October 2026 Indosat and F5 launched an AI services suite that sells model inference by the token.
platform: GPU Merdeka sells servers with eight NVIDIA H100 SXM GPUs, 3.2 Tbps of InfiniBand per server and racks of up to 20 kW. Zankore uses NVIDIA's DSX AI factory design with Nokia networking.
outlook: Zankore forecasts $13B of revenue over five years, and its first 200 MW must arrive in 2027 to start that plan. CoreWeave announced its own three data centers in Indonesia in August 2026, with 360 MW due online in 2028, and it named no Indonesian partner.

editor_notes: I found no relationship between CoreWeave and Indosat. CoreWeave's August 2026 Indonesia release says it will own and operate three sites with 360 MW of contracted power and names no local partner, so the owner's draft should not link the two. Zankore is the main 2026 development and may deserve its own entry. The founding year 2022 refers to the merger of Indosat Ooredoo and Hutchison 3 Indonesia, and the ownership line (Ooredoo and CK Hutchison control) comes from general knowledge, not from the listed sources. The $3.1B Zankore loan rests on Reuters and Data Center Dynamics headlines that I could not open. The F5 suite is described from its headline and a MarketScreener title that calls it a token factory.

name: darya.ai
snippet: Tajik startup that runs the country's first NVIDIA H200 cluster on hydropower in the Darvoz district and plans a green AI data center with India's Yotta, starting at 2 MW.

facts.label: First NVIDIA H200 cluster in Tajikistan

origin: darya.ai is a Tajik company that builds AI compute on Tajikistan's hydropower. It launched the country's first NVIDIA H200 cluster in June 2025 in the Darvoz district of Gorno-Badakhshan, and local press puts the cluster at 104 GPUs. It is one of five Tajik startups among the founding members of Tajikistan's AI special economic zone.
today: In October 2025 darya.ai signed an agreement with India's Yotta Data Services to build a green AI data center in Tajikistan, starting at 2 MW with room to grow to 100 MW. Tajik officials said the Darvoz data center would launch in 2026, and I found no 2026 update on its status.
platform: darya.ai offers clusters of NVIDIA GPUs to enterprises, government agencies, research groups and startups, powered entirely by hydropower.
outlook: The Yotta project is a multi-stage plan, and Darvoz is its first phase. Tajikistan has no established commercial data center market, so the project depends on new demand from the region.

I could not load darya.ai, and I found no founding year, founders, funding or 2026 news. name: Global AI
snippet: US provider of single-tenant, air-gapped GPU clusters for governments and enterprises. It says it runs New York State's largest GB300 NVL72 cluster and reports $6.2B of contracted revenue.

facts.label: Capacity roadmap
facts.value: 16 MW initial, 100 MW in 2026, 1 GW by 2029

origin: Sami Issa and John E. Kelly III founded Global AI in 2024 to build dedicated, air-gapped AI infrastructure for nations and enterprises. Its first data center in Endicott, New York runs liquid-cooled NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 clusters, and NVIDIA joined a funding round.
today: In March 2026 Global AI said it is deploying 7,000 GB300s at Endicott, starting from 16 MW of IT load and growing to 100 MW during 2026. In August 2026 it closed a $441M senior secured credit facility led by J.P. Morgan, its first debt raise, and reported $6.2B of contracted revenue. Humain agreed in November 2025 to develop large US AI data centers with Global AI.
platform: Global AI rents whole single-tenant environments, so customers never share bare metal or the software layer. The halls use direct-to-chip liquid cooling with rear-door heat exchangers. In July 2026 it passed NVIDIA's Exemplar Cloud validation for training on GB300 NVL72 at 512-GPU scale.
outlook: Global AI plans 250 MW for 2027 and 1 GW by 2029, and it plans Vera Rubin NVL72 systems next. It has not named its anchor customers or the sites beyond Endicott.

editor_notes: Identified as Global AI (globalai.com), the US sovereign AI infrastructure company that partnered with Humain in November 2025. Unrelated firms use similar names (globalai.co is an ESG data company). The HQ is set to Endicott, where its data center sits, and the corporate office may be elsewhere in New York. Global AI calls itself a sovereign AI hyperscaler and says it is not a multi-tenant neocloud, but its business is renting dedicated GPU clusters, so I used the neocloud category. The source says it is deploying 7000 GB300s without saying whether that counts GPUs or superchips. Customers beyond the Humain partnership are not public. The scale of contracted revenue relative to a 16 MW starting site is as reported by the company.
